look_here_first: START at a stem NODE: E. serpens is often a creeping plant that produces ADVENTITIOUS ROOTS at nodes in contact with soil. Look for a BROAD fused white-to-pink triangular stipule scale. Independent photo-proved characters: glabrous THREE-LOBED capsules and a smooth SEED without strong crosswise ribs. Contrast E. prostrata's hairy capsule KEELS and strongly transversely ridged seed. The installed 'flowering mat' image actually shows a CYATHIUM macro, not a full-plant mat. Node-root macro has noncommercial/source-restricted reuse and must be kept out of public website copy.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum sandmat: opposite leaves, milky latex, tiny cyathia, and 3-lobed capsules; habit, stipules, hairiness, fruit, and seed are the most useful field structures.

key_traits.label: Growth form
key_traits.text: Annual with slender taproot; stems strictly prostrate, frequently mat-forming and rooting at nodes, about 15–50 cm, glabrous. The local Williamson County treatment notes adventitious roots are commonly 1 or 2 per rooted node.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite; blades ovate, oblong, or orbiculate, usually 2–7(–9) × 2–6 mm; base asymmetric and rounded to subcordate; margins entire; apex rounded; surfaces glabrous and without a red blotch.

key_traits.label: Stipules
key_traits.text: Stipules are paired and fused across the node into conspicuous broad-deltate, white-to-pink membranous scales about 0.5–1(–1.2) mm; this fused scale is a major contrast with E. prostrata's upper-free/lower-fused pattern and E. villifera's distinct filiform stipules.

key_traits.label: Cyathium
key_traits.text: Cyathia solitary at distal nodes; 4 yellow oblong glands with small equal white-to-pink appendages forming a narrow rim at the gland edge.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Capsule broadly ovoid, oblate, or subglobose, about 1.3–1.4 × 1.3–1.7 mm, glabrous.

key_traits.label: Seed
key_traits.text: Seeds white to gray or light pink, ovoid, bluntly 3–4 angled in cross section, about 0.7–1.1 × 0.4–0.7 mm, smooth.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Strictly prostrate, low spreading annual with small opposite rounded leaves; not all photographed flower macros show mat habit.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Stems often put out adventitious ROOTS where nodes touch ground; evidence exists in historical research photo but that CC BY-NC-SA item is NOT eligible for public web distribution.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Broad triangular white-to-pink STIPULE SCALES are fused across nodes, unlike prostrata's partly free narrow stipules.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Stems and fruit essentially GLABROUS (without conspicuous hairs).

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Three-lobed glabrous capsule around 1.3–1.7 mm across.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Seeds approximately 0.7–1.1 mm with no strong transverse ridges; original 1 mm scale source photo covers surface.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Tiny cyathia with dark nectar glands and small white appendages; don't mistake them for four separate petals.

lookalikes.differences: Against E. prostrata: check a node first—serpens frequently roots there and has fused broad-deltate stipule scales; prostrata does not root at nodes and has an upper-free/lower-fused stipule pattern. Serpens is also glabrous with glabrous capsules and smooth seeds, while prostrata is crisped-villous with hairy capsule keels and ridged seeds. Against E. villifera, serpens is a glabrous rooted mat with fused scales; villifera is usually erect/ascending with distinct filiform stipules and papillate surfaces.
